title: Fibre geometry and regularity of a three-chart nodal gluing
statement:
Let $R$ be a DVR with uniformizer $\pi$ and $n\ge2$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. Let $Z$ be an $R$-scheme with an open cover by
$$U_x=\operatorname{Spec}R[x,t]/(xt-\pi),\quad U_m=\operatorname{Spec}R[r,s]/(rs-\pi^{n-2}),\quad U_y=\operatorname{Spec}R[y,h]/(yh-\pi)$$
[def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-polynomial-ring]. Assume the overlaps are $D(t)=D(r)$ with $r=t^{-1}$, $s=x^{n-2}t^{n-1}$, $x=\pi r$; $D(h)=D(s)$ with $s=h^{-1}$, $r=y^{n-2}h^{n-1}$, $y=\pi s$; and $D(x^{n-2}t^n)$ in $U_x$ for $U_x\cap U_y$, with $y=x^{n-1}t^n$, $h=\pi/y$ and the symmetric inverse. Then $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is flat and locally of finite presentation, with nonempty connected reduced one-dimensional nodal geometric fibres [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-trf-nodal-geometric-fibres]. Its generic fibre is the Laurent line. The outer charts are regular, and the only nonregular point of $Z$, if one exists, is the middle origin $(\pi,r,s)$ for $n\ge4$; its open local model is $\operatorname{Spec}R[r,s]/(rs-\pi^{n-2})$ [def-weil-regular-scheme]. For $n=2$ the middle chart is the smooth Laurent line $rs=1$, for $n=3$ it is regular, and in both cases $Z$ is regular. These fibre conclusions include connectedness after every algebraically closed extension, in arbitrary residue characteristic.

proof.text: Apply the DVR binomial local-geometry lemma with exponent $1$ to both outer chart rings and, when $n\ge3$, with exponent $n-2\ge1$ to the middle ring. These are flat $R$-algebras. For a point in one of these charts, the affine-stalk theorem identifies the structural stalk map with $R_{\mathfrak p}\to A_{\mathfrak q}$; the flat-map local criterion makes this map flat. If $n=2$, then $rs=1$, so $U_m=D(r)=U_m\cap U_x$ and the two outer charts already cover $Z$. Thus every structural stalk is flat, which is exactly flatness of $Z/R$. All three displayed chart rings, including $rs=1$, have two generators and one relation over $R$, so their affine neighbourhoods verify local finite presentation directly.

source.place: Tag 00HT (lemma-flat-localization), part (6); schemes.tex Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves), part (6); morphisms.tex Tags 01U3 (definition-flat), 01TP (definition-finite-presentation). Agent chartwise assembly.

proof.text: Fix an algebraically closed field $\Omega$ and a geometric point of $\operatorname{Spec}R$. A DVR has dimension one, is local and is a domain, so its only primes are $(0)$ and $(\pi)$. Write $a$ for the image of $\pi$ in $\Omega$; accordingly $a\ne0$ or $a=0$. The affine fibre-product theorem gives the fibre charts with rings $\Omega[x,t]/(xt-a)$, $\Omega[r,s]/(rs-a^{n-2})$ and $\Omega[y,h]/(yh-a)$, where the middle constant is $1$ for $n=2$. Explicitly the tensor-product identification sends $x\otimes1,t\otimes1,1\otimes\lambda$ to $x,t,\lambda$, and its inverse sends these generators back; the relation on each side is precisely the displayed relation. The pulled-back open charts cover the fibre, since every point maps into a chart of $Z$. Their pairwise intersections have the same equations and invertibility conditions as in the hypothesis: a map into a principal open is exactly a map on which its defining function is invertible.

source.place: Affine fibre-product construction; algebra.tex Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr). Agent substitution of the explicitly given presentations and overlaps.

proof.text: The binomial geometric-fibre lemma applies over $\Omega$ to each of the three constants in step 2, including $1$. It makes every chart nonempty, connected, reduced and of pure dimension one. It also says that a chart is smooth away from its crossing, and everywhere smooth when its constant is nonzero. The fibre is reduced because every local ring is a local ring of one of these reduced open charts. It has dimension at most one by the open-cover dimension theorem, applied to the scheme's sober underlying space; it has dimension at least one since the strict prime chain at an outer crossing when $a=0$, or a length-one chain in the outer Laurent line when $a\ne0$, remains a strict specialization chain in the whole fibre. At every crossing apply the monomial completion theorem with two variables and $J=(uv)$: its completed local ring is $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$. Stalks in an open chart are the ambient stalks. Smoothness is local on the source, so every nonsmooth point is one of the chart crossings just treated. This proves the reduced, one-dimensional and local nodal conditions in the definition.

source.place: Tag 0C59 (lemma-nodal-family) and Tag 0C5A (definition-nodal-family), local nodal conditions only; algebra.tex Tag 0315 (lemma-completion-generalities), through the explicit monomial completion node; topology.tex Tag 0B7I through the cited dimension node. Agent assembly, not an appeal to these tags for connectedness.

proof.text: The two adjacent intersections in the geometric fibre are nonempty. Indeed the first is $D(t)$ in the outer chart, with ring $\Omega[t,t^{-1}]$ and $x=a/t$, and the second is $D(h)$ with ring $\Omega[h,h^{-1}]$ and $y=a/h$. Their points $t=1$ and $h=1$ exist for every $a$, also in characteristic two. Each of the three charts is connected by step 3. If the fibre had a clopen partition, each chart would lie wholly in one part; the first adjacent intersection forces $U_x$ and $U_m$ into the same part, and the second forces $U_y$ into that part. Since the charts cover, the other part is empty. The nonempty charts also show that the fibre is nonempty. This argument applies to every chosen algebraically closed extension, so proves exactly the connectedness and nonemptiness demanded by the geometric-fibre definition.

source.place: Agent explicit connectedness proof for the stated reciprocal overlaps; Tag 0C59 (lemma-nodal-family) supplies no connectedness assertion.

proof.text: Put $K=\operatorname{Frac}R$. In all generic charts $\pi$ is a unit. Thus $x,t,r,s,y,h$ are units. Both adjacent intersections are therefore the entire respective generic charts: $D(t)=U_{x,K}$ and $D(r)=U_{m,K}$, and $D(h)=U_{y,K}$ and $D(s)=U_{m,K}$. Hence the open immersion $U_{x,K}\to Z_K$ is surjective and identifies the whole generic fibre with this one chart. Its ring is $K[t,t^{-1}]$ by $x=\pi/t$, as also given by the binomial geometric-fibre lemma. The middle and last coordinates are explicitly $r=t^{-1}$, $s=\pi^{n-2}t$, $y=\pi^{n-1}t$ and $h=\pi^{2-n}t^{-1}$; these obey both adjacent and the given outer-to-outer transition. Thus the identification is the asserted Laurent line, with all three generic charts identified compatibly.

source.place: Agent Laurent-coordinate calculation for the explicit overlaps; algebraic field-chart identification is supplied by the cited binomial geometric-fibre node.

proof.text: The DVR binomial local-geometry lemma at exponent $1$ says that every local ring in either outer chart is regular, including its origin. For $n\ge3$ apply the same lemma to the middle chart at exponent $e=n-2$. It is regular outside $(\pi,r,s)$ and regular at that point exactly when $e=1$. Hence $n=3$ gives a regular scheme, and for $n\ge4$ the middle origin is the only possible nonregular point; the middle open chart itself is its stated local model. These conclusions pass to $Z$ because open-chart and ambient local rings agree. For $n=2$, $U_m=D(r)$ lies in $U_x$ as in step 1, so regularity follows already from the outer charts. Moreover $R[r,s]/(rs-1)\cong R[r,r^{-1}]$, sending $s$ to $r^{-1}$. Its presentation $rs-1$ is standard smooth: the derivative with respect to $r$ is the unit $s$. The standard-smooth theorem and the ring-to-affine-scheme smoothness equivalence show that this middle Laurent line is smooth over $R$. All arguments used only a DVR and unit coefficients, imposing no residue-characteristic restriction.
